title: Detection of DNA damage by alkaline comet assay in mouse colonic mucosa
protocol: Place 1.5 mL labeled tubes with 500 μL of HBSS-EDTA on ice.
Longitudinally open the mice abdomen.
Collect the colon from the caecum to the rectum.
Wash the colon in a Petri dish full of 1× PBS.
Open the colon following a lengthwise axis.
Collect 0.5 cm of the distal part for comet assay.
Place the colon specimen on a microscope slide and scratch the mucosa using a scalpel blade.
Transfer the mucosal material in the tube containing 500 μL of HBSS-EDTA.
Place the tube back on ice.
Freeze samples within an hour after collection at −80°C.
Wait at least 24 hours before transferring tubes to a classical −80°C box.
Defrost samples approximately 2 hours at +4°C.
Keep the tubes on ice during defrosting.
Remove HBSS-EDTA buffer gently without centrifugation.
Add 750 μL of cold HBSS-EDTA buffer to the tissue.
Transfer the buffer containing the tissue to the Dounce tissue grinder.
Add 750 μL of cold HBSS-EDTA to the grinder for a final volume of 1.5 mL.
Mechanically dissociate cells 40 times up and down with the pestle.
Collect 15 μL of sample and dilute it with 15 μL of Trypan blue.
Determine the number of living cells using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the sample for 10 min at 200 g (slow brake around 2, +4°C).
Prepare positive and negative samples for your experiment in the same way.
Use cryopreserved aliquots from a single batch of peripheral blood mononuclear cells or mammalian cell lines.
Expose some cells to Methyl methanesulfonate (MMS) or ethyl methanesulfonate (EMS) as positive controls.
Incubate cells with 500 μM to 1 mM of MMS for 2 hours at 37°C.
Incubate cells with 5–10 mM of EMS for 2 hours at 37°C.
Include treated and untreated cells in agarose.
Deposit the cell-agarose mixture on Gelbond® film.
Place a metal plate on ice.
Position deposit patterns on top of the metal plate.
Put Gelbond® films in the holder if needed.
Annotate the Gelbond® films.
Position the annotated Gelbond® films on their patterns.
Discard the supernatant of the cells gently.
Add 300 μL of LMP agarose.
Mix gently using a pipette.
Load 15 μL of samples in duplicate or triplicate.
Transfer the holder with Gelbond® film to a container containing cold lysis solution.
Incubate for at least 1 hour at +4°C (can be prolonged overnight).
Place the holder with Gelbond® in a box containing electrophoresis solution at +4°C.
Cover with fresh and cold electrophoresis solution (+4°C).
Run the samples for 24 minutes at 28 V.
Put the Gelbond® in cold PBS (+4°C) for 5 min.
Repeat previous step (putting Gelbond® in cold PBS) one more time.
Soak the Gelbond® in cold absolute ethanol for 1.5 h at +4°C.
Cut the Gelbond® to adjust size to large microscope glass slides.
Glue the Gelbond® on a microscope glass slide.
Add 20 μL of SYBR Gold 1/10 in 20 mL of 1× TE buffer.
Incubate the slide with the glued Gelbond ® film in SYBR Gold solution sufficient to cover the slide for 20 min in darkness at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Rinse the slide with ddH2O.
Cover the slide with two rectangle coverslips.

Acquire images using a fluorescence microscope the same day (or after 1 night if kept in a humidified chamber at +4°C) with a FITC filter (emission wavelength 475 +/- 14 nm, transmission band: 500–550).
Scan slides using the Nikon NiS software at 20× magnification.
Pause point: Several pause points are possible but it is important to ensure that pause points are similar between different experiments inside the same project.
